name: Hiwa Feizi
title: Data Engineer
summary:
Data engineer at Allianz Netherlands. Driving the technical direction of a SAS-to-Snowflake migration. Leading an external 10+ person delivery team, owning the core upstream layer of the Data Office, and setting the AI tooling patterns the wider data org now uses across multiple country offices.

Strong in dbt, Snowflake, Python, SQL, and the surrounding cloud stack. The work I'm proudest of is the kind that makes whole teams faster. Automation that compounds, tooling other people adopt, decisions that hold up over time.

Background in cognitive science and AI. Before Allianz, shipped two production products solo on GCP with CI/CD (NeoCru, LinkInLead).

bullets.text: Allianz technical lead for a 10+ person IBM delivery team on the SAS-to-Snowflake migration: embedded in their daily standups, single escalation point for IBM-side issues, and the technical authority their design decisions ran through.

Drove validation and data-movement design changes IBM adopted; owned acceptance criteria, dbt code review, and model-design review; coordinated across IBM, the SAS team, IT, and the Data Office; mentored a junior Allianz engineer.
Defined the SAS team's tasks throughout the migration and gave them targeted dbt/Snowflake training as needed, enabling them to validate parity from the SAS side.
Owned technical decisions on pstag, the Data Office's upstream source: reviewed pull requests, validated results against data, set the team's PR standards, and proposed enhancements to the project.
Defined the SAS-migration source-loading strategy and co-designed new ingestion processes with IT for previously missing sources.

Built a generic Python parser for the mainframe PD binary format after spotting data loss in the prior CSV ingestion. Switched input to binary while keeping CSV output, added batching and structured logging, and moved per-table config to JSON files in the repo so changes ship through version control instead of IT tickets.

Built an AI-driven SAS↔Snowflake column matching pipeline: chains LLM API calls with live SAS and Snowflake connections, parses metadata, samples row-level values, and validates matches programmatically. Reached 93% average accuracy and became what the team uses to validate the migration and review dbt developers' PRs.
Crawled SAS server directories to extract transformation logic from 1,000+ SAS files, cataloguing reusable code to accelerate the migration of legacy pipelines to dbt on Snowflake.
Migrated pstag from script-based logic to dbt models and YAML configurations; programmatically generated ~660 YAML files and 2,000+ SQL models using Python and Snowflake metadata.
Built a validation framework using dbt macros and runtime checks, achieving 100 percent row- and column-level parity against production for daily data loads exceeding 50 million rows.

Built an API over Azure Blob Storage that streams and analyzes 20+ GB files in place (no full download), producing cross-table data-quality reports in seconds and flagging source issues to fix at the source.

Automated recurring data-engineering work against the Snowflake API at scale: zero-copy clones for source-specific schemas, parallel test/data extraction, and Python-threaded data manipulation with structured logging.

Designed and implemented an automated documentation system that extracts and structures raw-level metadata from multi-format, multi-language source files into table-based documentation across three languages.
Co-designed and implemented reusable dbt macros for automated table and view generation, standardizing transformations across schemas.
Operate dbt Cloud as the team's orchestration layer: scheduled jobs, ad-hoc runs, and CI/CD pipelines for development and production deployments.

Got Claude Code adopted across the Data Office: built a shared data-engineering agent with council-style review and plan-before-code baked into its context (used by 20+ engineers), working demos for data engineering and data science, and an end-to-end setup guide (permissions, configuration, VS Code integration) used by engineers in multiple Allianz country offices.

Built a context-locked AI workflow for onboarding new sources to the pipeline: tasks estimated at 8 hours now take 5 minutes of AI work plus 5 to 55 minutes of validation. Predefined deliverables (three SQL files, one YAML, dbt commands, validation queries) make the result identical run to run and let engineers with no prior pipeline knowledge debug it.
Helped peer technical leads on other teams build their own agents on Allianz's internal AI platform and adopt Snowflake-API automation patterns for their projects.
Proposed and implemented a new data processing architecture that reduced end-to-end pipeline runtime by ~99 percent, cutting execution time from ~1.5 days to minutes.
Rebuilt undocumented Oracle SQL pipelines into dbt models on Snowflake, achieving >=99.9 percent data accuracy, with ~70 percent of tables reaching full parity across millions of rows.
Simplified the data architecture by removing redundant processing steps, reducing compute costs and maintenance overhead.
Built a Power BI dashboard to monitor dbt Cloud runs with hierarchical filtering and enriched metadata for improved operational visibility.

Built an AI-assisted recruitment platform solo, end to end: Flask/PostgreSQL backend, recruiter dashboards with role-based access, and OpenAI-driven job-description generation for Dutch businesses running without full HR systems.

Ran it as a production system on GCP: containerized Cloud Run services, Cloud Build CI/CD, Cloud Storage for applicant resumes, and structured logging, the same deploy discipline I'd expect at work, applied to my own product.
Killed it deliberately in Dec 2025 and shut the company down properly, KVK deregistration included. The full reasoning is in the post-mortem.

Built an automation platform that generates and publishes LinkedIn content end to end: LinkedIn API integration, OpenAI text generation, and scheduled publishing behind user accounts with secure session management.
Designed the orchestration layer to run without daily attention: Cloud Functions and Cloud Tasks running scheduled content creation and background jobs, deployed as containerized services with CI/CD.
Retired it after a year; its Cloud Tasks orchestration pattern became the direct ancestor of the Meme Factory pipeline's self-scheduling task loader.

projects.name: Mad Pod Racing - A Learned Game Bot in the World Top 500

bullets.text: Reached 459th of 233,508 (top 0.2%) on CodinGame's Mad Pod Racing world leaderboard with a learned bot: PPO self-play, DAgger imitation, and league evolution.
Rebuilt the game physics as a GPU-vectorized PyTorch simulator averaging 600 games per second on one consumer RTX 4060: the throughput behind all 29 experiments.
Iterated the reward function against turn-by-turn visualizations of games and reward signals, raising the win rate against the fixed hand-coded benchmark bot from 18% to 100%.
Built a dedicated defender bootcamp with adversarial spawns and urgency-weighted rewards, turning near-certain breaches into full-lap holds.
Kept networks tiny and training short by engineering the inputs (calculated features in, noise excluded) instead of hoping a bigger net would sort it out.
Shipped the whole system (nets, weights, geometry) as one self-contained Python file with embedded weights trimmed to fit CodinGame's submission limit.

projects.name: LinkedIn Meme Factory - Automated Content Pipeline

bullets.text: Built a Python pipeline that generates niche-specific LinkedIn meme content with Grok, validates each batch through a second LLM pass against a per-template humor model in a 1,000-line catalog, and renders 20 PIL meme templates.

Designed two execution modes sharing one codebase: eager pre-rendering with direct Cloud Tasks scheduling, and lazy on-demand rendering inside a GCP Cloud Function, driven by a self-perpetuating task loader that queues a day of Cloud Tasks and then schedules itself for tomorrow.

Ran it fully autonomously across 3 LinkedIn business pages for a pre-registered 100-day window, posting twice a day. Total Grok cost: $0.34. Engagement was effectively zero; the 10-niche fan-out the architecture was built for was blocked by LinkedIn's business-page limits. Wrote the post-mortem with full cost data anyway.

projects.name: Half Stupid - Teaching Minecraft Agents to Survive From Scratch

bullets.text: Built a dual-timescale neural network (reflex layer at every tick, context layer every 5 ticks) using shared learned embeddings across 2048 block/item/entity types, processing 557 raw inputs into 23 actions with zero human-labeled knowledge.

Trained with vanilla REINFORCE on a survival-only reward (+1 alive, -10,000 on death) and got emergent food-seeking, distinct agent personalities, and inter-agent social dynamics without any reward shaping.
Closed the project on evidence: profiled the Minecraft/Malmo substrate to a hard 4-agent, ~4,000 ticks/sec ceiling, quantified that further training was compute-starved, and stopped there.

projects.name: Thesis - Predicting Perceptions of Dutch Company Names

bullets.text: Built an end-to-end pipeline predicting human trait judgments (femininity, evilness, trustworthiness, smartness) from Dutch brand-like names, aggregating Bayesian posterior samples from raw ranking experiments into stable regression targets.
Engineered three feature pipelines: character-level unigrams (27D), padded bigrams (479D), and contextual RobBERT embeddings (768D).
Trained and evaluated 64+ models (Elastic Net and feedforward networks) across in-domain, out-of-domain, and few-shot splits with fixed seeds and consistent R² evaluation.
Multimodal speech recognition with AV-HuBERT: built the lip-extraction and audio-video alignment pipeline and a parallelized inference setup processing 21,000+ audio/video files.
PetMatters: led a team of 8 building a multi-service AI application; trained and integrated T5 models for English-to-Dutch translation and form-driven content generation.
Battle-C: modular C++ game engine with AI opponent logic and real-time state tracking.
Wildfire-risk prediction: LightGBM pipeline modeling fire outbreak risk from environmental data.
